content.text:
**Finding submitted — IP (deviation, fallback target).**

- **Ownership direction is fine**: 11.1(a)/(b) leave each Party owning what it solely creates; nothing assigns Ono IP or data to Array.
- **The failure is 11.1(d)**: joint ownership (11.1(c)) is paired with internal-use-only practice and a mutual consent gate on enforcing, licensing or assigning joint IP — joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit (walk-away), and short of the fallback's perpetual/irrevocable/worldwide/royalty-free use-modify-sublicense right.
- **Cure (2 surgical ops, validated ok:true)**: (1) free Ono's side of 11.1(d) with the fallback licence wording, expressly subject to Section 2.1(d) so the no-modification covenant survives, and leaving the inter-party licence carve-out and Array's consent restriction untouched; (2) a one-sentence proviso limiting the Section 2.6 Grant-Back Licence, insofar as it reaches Data/Ono Know-How, to Array's performance of its obligations under the Agreement.
- Preferred (deleting joint ownership) was rejected because it would require collateral rewrites of the Joint Invention/Patent/Know-How definitions, 11.2(b) and the Article II licences.
